headline: Pretrained protein language model embeddings drive task-specific bioactivity prediction
label: Protein Language Model Prediction
summary: Recent 2026 papers pair pretrained protein language model embeddings with graph, contrastive, and attention heads for diverse prediction tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representation from sequence feeding task-specific prediction heads. Several items use pretrained protein language model embeddings directly as input: BAN-SDBPred (ESM2, ProtT5), SDGT, ToxMamba (ISM embeddings), EvoGraph, and DeepIR-Pred. A benchmark study evaluates such embeddings within graph-based drug-target affinity prediction on Davis and KIBA against CNN baselines. What is new is the pairing of these embeddings with specific inductive biases: tail-aware graph contrastive learning in EvoGraph, Siamese contrastive learning in PhoSARte, bilinear or cross-attention fusion in BAN-SDBPred, DualBAN, and Bi-MHA, and multi-scale state-space modeling in ToxMamba. Other items, including CliffRank, DFRL-Mol, PEARL, and ReMol, address ranking, molecule optimization, target recommendation, and molecular image learning, so the thread is dominant rather than universal.
